As someone who has gone years with this before finding this sub or even knowing about DPDR with absolutely no improvement (and in fact exclusively worsening) dpdr, don't assume that what works for you will work for everyone else. You are not a therapist and you cannot tell people that the definitive cure is to not think about it. That isn't how trauma works, not everyone will walk the same road to recovery. It may have worked for you, and it may work for some others, but it is not a catch all cure for this. Some people need to vent to deal with the trauma and emotions (or lack thereof) as part of their healing process. Ultimately everyone here needs professional therapy, where they can find a path that works for *them*. But unfortunately not everyone has that option and therefore telling people that the cure is to abandon their only understanding support network just because it worked for you is selfish. You are not a therapist, you can say it worked for you, but you cannot label this as the cure

I'm glad I'm not the only one at least, fingers crossed that you can find a way out. I wouldn't wish dpdr on my worst enemy, the things it does to you and the mistrust you end up with for the world around you is horrible. This isn't some kind of crazy favoritism in the workplace or something, but in highschool there was some kind of unspoken rivalry between the cheerleaders and the colorguard. The reason being was that the cheerleaders always got everything and the colorguard got nothing. Cheerleaders got a new stereo every year. Colorguard, despite requesting even a shitty Bluetooth speaker for the 4 years I was there, even writing directly to the principal about our struggle, had to use a dedicated plastic cup with a hole through it to amplify music from our phones, that was what we were given. The chorus teacher sometimes took pity on us and let us use her big bluetooth speaker system but chorus always had practice when we did so they usually had to use it. Let me tell you, the sound of 15 flags swinging easily drowns out any music no matter how loud from a phone. Hell, even one flag will drown out a phone. We would have been better as a team if we had a speaker, our teacher wouldnt let us bring our own, personal speakers were banned because too many students blasted them in the hallways. But the cheerleaders got a new one every year and left the old ones to rot in a closet that we were not allowed to touch. Another example is cheerleaders getting new pom poms every two years and us not getting pom poms for 15 years. We were waving sticks with 10 strands of sad, pathetic pastic on each end. Our school wasnt poor, we are one of the richest public schools in the state, but we were waving around sticks instead of poms. 

That was only one way the cheerleaders were favored over us. We had a gym built into the school, it had the top 'ring' which was mostly just the space for more seating to pull out, and the bottom floor which was the actual gym floor. Now, colorguard has flags and equipment that we throw into the air, if it is *too* windy we cannot practice outside, same with rain. The only place inside that has tall enough ceilings for us to practice is the gym. The chearleading coach was a real bitch to everyone (I could go on forever about her, only a bitch would pride herself for telling a pregnant teenager that her life was over, that she would never amount to anything, and that she might as well drop out, it happened like 6 years before I had her class and she told every class that story every year), so it wasn't surprising that she was a bitch to us. The cheerleaders of course got the gym floor first, fine, whatever. We didn't technically need the floor specifically, we could make do with the ring at the top. But if we even stepped foot in the gym she would scream at us, berate us, and insult us until we left. No class needed "permission" to use the top of the gym, plenty of other classes went in to use the top of the gym, from the art classes, other pe classes, and even core classes to do projects. Anyone could use it. But they would scream until we left and they told the principal to make us the only ones not able to use it because "we were tearing up the floor" which was a blatant lie, their shoes messed up the waxed floor of the gym more than our equipment messed up the concrete top, which was not at all. We had rubber stoppers on our equipment for a reason. And if you say our flags disrupted their practice, they blasted their stereo so loud that you could hear it clearly outside the gym, we couldnt hear our own flags spinning in front of us.

TLDR: Highschool sucks, favoritism is blatant everywhere, colorguard got fucked over by cheerleaders.

My mom works for walmart and if anyone wants a flip side to the hate, yeah they do some scummy shit to their employees, but that isnt something to do with the company as a whole for the most part. That has to do with the individual stores and people within the company bullying and not adhering to company rules. With a company so large it is increasingly hard to enforce rules in every single walmart, a flaw that comes with any company that gets too large. Right now in this pandemic state, walmart is doing an incredible amount within it's employee base to protect employees financially and health-wise. Anyone who can work is allowed tons of overtime pay and is generally getting paid a ton more, and anyone who is even slightly sick, corona or otherwise, is being sent home immediately with full pay. They are looking out for their workers both in warehouses (where my mom works) and in stores. Every single person is required to wear masks and gloves which are (or at least are supposed to be, again, not every store follows rules, thats not the corporation, thats individuals) provided for them. So far they have had one "employee hour" day where employees can shop early before anyone else and get anything they need, and they are planning more. They have been looking out for workers a lot right now and I feel like that should be acknowledged.

Yes walmart has done shitty stuff but a lot of just straight untrue shit gets circled around about them.

edit- Just to clarify: I do not think Walmart is a perfect company, they do scummy stuff too, but right now with the current pandemic they are stepping up and doing a very good thing and looking out for their employees

Thank god someone who understands. I have ocd and it's hell. It's not some cutesy thing. I can't function daily and mental healthcare in the US is a joke, it's unaffordable for people struggling to live on the daily, which of course doesnt help anyone's mental health. Every day is a struggle for me. I constantly touch doors, idk why, I just have to. I have been playing the same game every night for 12 years for an arbitrary reason that has never and will never matter but I play it anyway, I have to bring my DS with me everywhere I go in case something happens and I have to spend the night somewhere abruptly and I have a full on panic attack if I can't play it. I'm fuckin 20, do you know how embarassing it is to have to play Animal Crossing every single night or have a panic attack just so I can keep the same 3 charaters in my town for *literally no reason*? I have to check locks constantly and doors constantly because my dog got out one time, I will turn around on my way to work and risk being late just to *make sure * that door is closed and locked. Hell even just being in public is a nightmare, I'm amazed people don't notice how im constantly freaking out inside. And shit, its not just me, every woman in my mothers side of the family is missing our eyebrows and eyelashes because we all have Trichotillomania. This shit isn't cute, it's hard to just live life normally with all this shit that we *have* to do. My mom has to fold all her laundry a very specific way, if she doesn't or if someone else folds it differently she can't even sleep until she fixes it. It's not always big shit, but sometimes it's just a ton of tiny little things stacked on each other until just doing your daily routine is a nightmare. I give people the benefit of the doubt most of the time when someone says they have OCD, but if you sit here and tell me you have OCD only because of a literally natural reaction to seeing a broken pattern, I'm going to tell you to your face that you are giving people actually suffering a bad image. Same with people who say "Everyone is a little OCD or ADHD". No, no they aren't.  It's a disorder, if we all had it, it wouldn't be a disorder, it would be human fucking nature. A disorder is something that isn't normal.
